Rally,then Wood (16)
4 Build Council Hall Villager,then Sheep. Queue Spearman and Longbowman. Wait with them in your base until you have 2 Spearmen and 3 Longbowmen
1 Wood Villager,then Build House
Once you have 2 Spearmen and 3 Longbowmen, move out of your base towards enemy Gold to deny either Knight production or fast Castle Age

Those units are enough to catch isolated Knight and force them to run away, that way the cavalry player will have to completely ignore you or to commit with all of their units, likely loosing one or two (depending on micro) in the process. This will heavily delay the raids, building a lot of time for you and your team to stablish proper defenses. It's ok to loose these units as long as they can make time.
Feudal Age All-in:

If you are playing with an ally making Feudal Age Knight and want to commit to an all-in, keep making Longbowman and Spearman. Build Blacksmith and move 4 Wood Villager to Gold once you start floating Wood. Research: Double Broadax,then Steeled Arrow,then Iron Undermesh,then Siege Engineering,then Wheelbarrow,then Horticulture
Transition to Castle Age:
Keep making Spearman at home to defend.
Build House as needed and slowly move Sheep Villager to Farm
Once you finish the first pack of Farm, build Palisade Wall, Rally to Gold and gradually add more Farm, but this time with Wood Villager
16 Farms are more than enough to make units and quickly get to Castle Age
10 Food Villager,then Build Castle Age

King's Palace: Allows you to catch up in economy to the opponents who started with a second Town Center. Since you have a decent amount of Spearman defending, you should not need the inmediate protection of the other landmark. The White Tower: Since we already have Spearman to defend and Council Hall to quickly produce units, most of this landmark's value is lost in this build order.
You need at least 15 Villagers on Gold by the time you reach Castle Age to get upgrades. Move Wood Villager to Gold if necessary. Once you have 15 on Gold, Rally to Wood
Upgrade Spearman, produce Spearman and Crossbowman, and research economic upgrades ( Wheelbarrow, Specialized Pick, Double Broadax, Horticulture )
Add another Barracks and then Build more Farm, Outpost and Palisade Wall

Once you have a strong army to push and some Blacksmith upgrades, mine Stone with 5 Gold Villager and Build Outpost wherever you expect you will be fighting in the future (i.e. next to large Gold, in front of your allies' bases, etc.).

title: New Player Guide to Japanese

There are 2 recommended choices once you complete the below build and attack: 1. Go all-in with aggression! title: Japanese | FC cavalry
description: Fast Castle build order with tips for team games. It works best if there are no HRE, OotD or Zhu'Xi players (on either team), and it relies on your teammates putting pressure on the oponents in Feudal Age. Still, it works as a standard build even if you have to delay the age-up thanks to the yorishiros, onna-musha and mounted samurai. Other japanese builds: - 2TC: https://aoe4guides.com/builds/BKgxe5CAXfcRTj4Sbq5C - Feudal all-in: https://aoe4guides.com/builds/0AloblREG8fqZjucs0AU
author: Jockxtar
steps: Since you won't rely on Sheep, use Scout to go deep into the enemy side of the map, try to steal their Sheep and check their landmarks.
5 Villagers,then Sheep. 1 Villager,then build Farmhouse at Berries
Rally,then Gold (2). First one builds Forge
Rally,then Sheep (10)
Rally,then Straggler Tree (5)
3 Sheep Villager build Kura Storehouse (preferably 2 tiles away from Town Center and next to Wood )
Of the 3 Villagers Build Kura Storehouse: 2 to Gold and 1 to the generated Farm upon completion.
2 Sheep Villager,then Gold
Farmhouse,then Tawara
Build Farmhouse at Berries
Rally,then Sheep (16)
Scout Scout enemies that may try to all-in you
Farmhouse,then Takezaiku. Forge,then Specialized Pick

Build Barracks to make 4 Spearmen against French Jeanne d'Arc Mongols Rus English ( Abbey of Kings ). You may also build short Palisade Wall to cut off rotations around your base. OR. Build Outpost on Gold against English ( Council Hall ) Byzantines Ayyubids Zhu Xi's Legacy (scout their base and check if they are making Longbowman, Desert Raider or Zhuge Nu ). If you are being harassed by both types of units, do not hesitate to do both things (put more villagers on Wood temporarily). Surviving is more important than rushing the age up.
Move all Sheep Villager,then Berries
Move 1 Berries Villager to Farm as they generate from Kura Storehouse
Build Lumber Camp
Build Stable
Rally,then Gold (10). Build Farmhouse around Farm
Daimyo Manor before aging up to make a Uma Bannerman
10 Food Villager,then Castle Age

Floating Gate: For faster Mounted Samurai or Onna-Musha production in early Castle Age and adding passive income. At this point it's possible that there are no Relic left, but if there are, try to get them with the free Shinto Priest. Temple of Equality: Only good if your team has been putting a lot of pressure on the enemies and most Relic are still unclaimed. This landmark unlocks cheap Buddhist Monk, which allows picking up several very quickly. Buddhist Monk are also decent against Order of the Dragon units and Delhi Sultanate elephants.
Build Archery Range
Make 1 Uma Bannerman. If you don't need it to defend, move it to raid the enemy base.
Rally,then Wood (30)
Ideal army composition: Mounted Samurai + Handcannon Ashigaru + Uma Bannerman + Yumi Bannerman. Add Onna-Bugeisha + Katana Bannerman vs Spearman + Crossbowman. Add Spearman vs Horseman Knight
10 Castle Age Villager,then Food. Shinto Priest yorishiro in order,then Archery Range / Stable (only one), main Town Center, Forge, Forge
Keep building Farmhouse at Farm

Keep the Archery Range and Stable constantly making Onna-Musha and Mounted Samurai. Separate a handful of Mounted Samurai for raiding opponent's economy while your main army runs around the map taking small trades against enemy reinforcement's or counter-raiding (protecting yourself and your allies). Remember to always keep a Scout and Uma Bannerman with your army.
Build Forge at Stone with 3 Wood Villager
Research Fudasashi and Forge upgrades

Make Daimyo Palace. After which you can decide how to balance your army between cavalry ( Uma Bannerman ) and melee infantry ( Katana Bannerman ). Ideally you want to separate it on thirds. So, for example, 1/3 Onna-Musha, 1/3 Mounted Samurai / Horseman and 1/3 melee infantry would mean 1 Katana Bannerman and 2 Uma Bannermen.
Slowly save up Wood and Stone for second Town Center. If your Wood goes over 500, build additional military buildings and Farm
Build Shinto Shrine if you manage to get any Relic

Once you have done enough damage and your economy has scaled, you should be ready to go for an all-in, forcing the enemies to take fights where you are constantly trading units. This will keep them locked in Castle Age, allowing you to finish the Farm transition and even to get Shogunate Castle for an insane Food economy. Also, it doesn't matter what strategy your allies are going for, they will be able to eventually join you in the all-in since you are creating a long engagement with your opponents.

Tanegashima Gunsmith: Is the standard. Always good no matter what. Getting free Handcannon Ashigaru and Ozutsu adds a lot of firepower to your main army with just 1 Yumi Bannerman, no further investment is needed for them to work. Ribauldequin are excellent at defending against big groups of melee units. And Bombard are excellent at finishing off opponents. Castle of the Crow: Is very strong in the late stages of the game to protect key resources in the middle of the map or to secure chokepoints. The additional resources are also nothing to scoff at. 210 Food Wood Gold and 70 Stone per minute is the equivalent to 9 Relic split into all 4 resources.

Ideal army composition: Mounted Samurai + Handcannon Ashigaru + Uma Bannerman + Yumi Bannerman. Add Onna-Bugeisha + Katana Bannerman vs Spearman + Crossbowman. Add Spearman vs Horseman Knight. Add Bombard to finish the game. A combination of Naginata Samurai, Onna-Bugeisha and Katana Bannerman works great as an efficient meat shield for your Mounted Samurai and Handcannon Ashigaru.
See to the left. Economy balance should look like this.
Military buildings proportions: 15 Barracks; 5 Archery Ranges; 10 Stables; 1 Siege Workshop
Since the japanese gain additional Stone when mining Gold and viceversa, and your army is very Gold heavy, researching Cupellation after your military "elitency" upgrades is very much worth it.

Research Bunrei at a Shinto Shrine and place the two new yorishiros at Forge. Additionally, you may delete the Stable / Archery Range holding the first yorishiro to place the replacement on a Siege Workshop. Getting siege units and their upgrades faster can be crucial in the late stages of the game.

title: Detailed Cheese Men-At-Arms guide (BeastyqtSC2)
description: I decided to make this guide a bit more detailed for new players. (this is my first guide)
author: Juny Foo
steps: Summary (in order): - 3 villagers on wood. - 1 villager on house,then then join wood. - 1 villager on mill,then then build farm. - 1 villager on farm. ---. - Create 6 villagers to go on farm. ---. - 4 villagers from wood to gold. - Create 2-4 villagers to go on sheep (last step before Abbey of kings)
The very first thing you should do: Let Town Center to Build Villager (this action should be non-stop throughout the game)

You'll start by moving your 6 starting villagers accordingly: 3 Villagers queue 2x Straggler Tree. 1 Villager to Build House,then queue 2x Straggler Tree. 1 Villager to Build Mill,then queue Build Farm. 1 Villager to Build Farm. *Villagers will build mills next to the mill. *The single villager who built the house will be queued to join the other 3 villagers harvesting the 2 straggler trees

These actions will be done over a few minutes: Rally 6 Villagers from Town Center to Build Farm (this should result in having all 8 farms around your mill). while you wait for your villagers: Queue your scout to circle your base, eventually grabbing sheep to bring back to the Town Center. You can also go and scout out your gold deposits.
Once you have 8 farms built, and you have 50 wood, then: 4 Villagers from Wood to Build Mining Camp to gather Gold (your villagers should be done harvesting the 2 trees by now)
At this point: you'll end up waiting for you 4 villagers to gather 200 gold, while you wait go ahead and... Rally Town Center to Sheep
Once you get 400 food and 200 gold then: Move 4 Villagers from Gold to Build Abbey of Kings

Your next goal is to get 8 villagers on wood while your Abbey of Kings landmark is getting constructed: Rally Town Center to Wood (Rallying to the straggler tree next to Town Center). Move Villager from Sheep to harvest Straggler Tree next to Town Center

Once you have 50 wood: Move Villager from Straggler Tree to build Lumber Camp to harvest Wood. *Make sure your lumber camp is built next to an abundant supply of wood. *Don't forget to re-rally wood from Straggler tree next to the town center to wood next to the lumber camp
Build House
Once you have 8 Villagers on wood: Rally 2 Villagers from Town Center to Gold
Your Abbey of Kings should be completed: Move Villager from Abbey of Kings to Gold
1 Villager from Town Center to Build queue 2 Barracks. Rally Villager from Town Center to Build Farm and Mill
Build Man-at-Arms from Barracks (this should theoretically non stop for the rest of the game)

The world is your oyster, what happens next is up to you. I recommend practicing this build order against an easy ai a few times to get comfortable with it. (or watch Beasty's video). I didn't expect creating a guide would take so much effort, I'm just a noob player in AOE4. Once i play this strategy enough, I'll change it up, add or remove some things. Let me know if I did something wrong, if theres an error, or if it's too hard to follow. I originally wanted to create something more readable and understandable to the average new player, but I'm afraid I've made a considerable block of confusing instructions.

Move Scholar near Relic to grab them as soon as you age up. Again, don't be greedy. The priority is to not loose them.
Make additional Scout to steal Deer from the opponent's side of the map, securing food and delaying the farm transition.

Try to extend this age for as much as possible, giving you time to get all the upgrades, a bunch of keeps to boost your economy and lots of scholars. Add Ghazi Raider / Lancer to raid and to mess up with the opponent's composition, forcing them into Spearman. Add Spearman / War Elephant against Lancer

Rally,then Food (30) and Gold (16) in that order
Produce a few Lancer to distract, raid and force the opponents to make Spearman. Attack quickly and frequently to prevent the opponents from aging up.
Build 6 Barracks, 6 Archery Ranges and 3 Stables with excess Wood. Build 1 Siege Workshop and garrison 1 Scholar inside. That will be enough until late Imperial Age.
If you have control of Sacred Site, produce additional Scholar (up to 15).

As you get Stone, build Keep to protect key resources in the middle of the map and Stone Wall to protect your base. Build Mosque behind Keep to benefit from the healing from Tranquil Venue. 3 Keeps is a good amount to stop gathering Stone. After that move Stone Villager,then Wood and start the farm transition.
See to the left. Ideal economy (for now) should look like this
After technologies are done, garrison Scholar inside military buildings.
Build House around Farm to garrison Villager if raided.

Hisar Academy for faster tempo (much faster late game upgrades) and better food economy. Allows you to liberate population space for a bigger army. Palace of the Sultan good when constantly fighting/trading units with the opponents.
Make Scholar up to 20, but don't build more Mosque (unless you want them in forward positions to heal units).

Ideal army composition: Man-at-Arms + Handcannon Ashigaru + Mangonel. Add Springald to counter enemy siege. (Although your allies should make Culverin ). Add Ghazi Raider to raid and to mess up with the opponent's composition, forcing them into Spearman. Add War Elephant against Lancer

Garrison Scholar inside Hisar Academy / Madrasa (including the 3 that spawn outside of it). Research Elite Army Tactics Chemistry Biology Siege Works Court Architects Incendiary Arrows. Research all upgrades.
After unit upgrades and economic technologies are completed: Garrison Scholar inside military buildings.
Build Palisade Wall with your units as you push into the opponent's side of the map to protect reinforcements and control resources.
Military buildings proportions: 10 Barracks; 10 Archery Ranges; 4 Stables; 1 Siege Workshop

author: SuperTTB
steps: Intro BO Abbasid Dynasty simple et efficace. Villager x6 to Berries / moulin, Scout cherche Sheep.

Cliquer Military Wing Aile militaire. Donne 2 archers + 2 piquiers gratuitement au passage age 2.
Une fois Military Wing cliquee: tous les Villager des Sheep vont sur Wood. Rally du TC sur Wood.
Conseil micro: idealement 5 Villagers par arbre pour eviter les retours inefficaces. Le 6e peut partir sur un autre arbre.
Construire une nouvelle House dans l'aura de House of Wisdom. Chercher vite l'Age d'or: 10 batiments = +15% recolte.
Construire Lumber Camp et House. Preparer assez de Wood pour sortir rapidement Stable.
Passage age 2 avec Military Wing: recevoir 2 Archers + 2 Spearmen gratuits.
Construire Stable le plus vite possible avec 4 Villagers. But: sortir Horseman pour contrer les archers adverses.
Les 4 builders de Stable vont a Food. Viser environ 10 Villagers sur nourriture; Rally TC reste sur Wood.
Lancer Fresh Foodstuffs apres Wheelbarrow pour payer les Villager moins cher.
Tech eco: commencer Horticulture, puis Double Broadax selon le nombre de Villager.
Ajouter Archery Range rapidement. En meme temps construire House pour atteindre l'Age d'or.
Quand Archery Range est lancee, ajouter directement une autre House si besoin pour debloquer l'Age d'or (+15% recolte).
Pression avec combo Horseman + Archer, protege par les Spearman gratuits. Forcer l'adversaire a produire.
Priorite: House avant Blacksmith si cela donne l'Age d'or. La forge peut etre delay un peu.
Tech militaire: Iron Undermesh / resistance fleches souvent avant Steeled Arrow si l'adversaire a des unites a distance.
Option pression: avec Military Wing, faire rapidement Battering Ram avec archers/piquiers sans attendre expertise de siege si l'adversaire ne repond pas bien.
Adaptation: contre cavalerie lourde, commencer Stable puis Archery Range, et ajouter Barracks si besoin.
Si trop de Wood: faire Outpost, moulins sur ressources externes, ou transitions eco. Continuer la pression et le controle carte.

Sword Hunt Statue: The increase to the Daimyo attack speed aura makes Sengoku Daimyo army insanely strong. By far the best option. Castle of the Crow: Good in closed maps with key chokepoints. Overall quite weaker in team games.

Tanegashima Ashigaru are a good addition to the army since they are ranged units and benefit a lot from the bonus attack speed of Daimyo. Ikko Ikki Monk are also a great addition to the frontline, since they can heal the whole army every time they attack and can become quite tanky with upgrades, and they don't receive bonus damage from either Archer or Crossbowman.
Last but not least, research Oda Tactics and Serpentine Powder as well as Samurai Bow and Buddhist Temple upgrades.

title: Jin FC taking outside hunt
description: This build is for situations where you will not get harrassed in dark age and preferably early feudal and uses 5 mounted villagers to collect deer on the map and get the food for FC, saving the food under your TC for later. After the initial mounted villagers, you make normal villagers to spend the food and to not deplete your initial gold too fast. I chose to go up with Great Pasture and Mountain Hall to be able to spam Grassland Iron Pagodas and Monks upon age-up and compete for the relics. With this build you can spam Iron Pagoda's almost continuously using only Grassland horses (so with 25 food discount and instant training). This is because the horses spawn faster in Castle Age and you have already 3 grasslands (incl. Great Pasture). If you like this build or you have any suggestions, leave a comment :)
author: Flip
steps: Queue 2 Mounted Villagers, then Villager. Three starting Mounted Villager go on Gold, build Mining Camp with 1. Rally on Deer under TC.
Drop off food (should be able to queue 3 vills now), take all 5 Mounted Villagers and Build Mill on Deer. Research Mohe Ancestry.
Next 2 Villagers go on straggler tree Wood to collect 50 for a House.
Rally next Villager on Gold. When you have 50 Wood, Build House and go on Gold with these vills.

As for placement of the landmarks: your Mountain Hall will need to be close to Town Center to have most resources in its aura. You want your Great Pasture close to the eventual Mountain Hall position to maximise the chance the Mountain Hall Grassland will spawn in range of the Great Pasture.
You will have enough to age up with Great Pasture. Take 2 from Gold and rally 1 more from TC.

Then Rally to the already cut straggler tree to gather 100 Wood for Grassland. These villagers will move to Gold after finishing the tree, so you can shift-queue the rally point from the tree to the gold. When the tree finishes, Rally on Wood (next straggler) for the next 3 Villagers, we will need a House.
Aim for this distribution just before reaching Feudal Age.
1 Build Grassland, other builders go on Gold. Rally Gold.
1 Wood villager builds House just before 20 pop. TC Rally on Food.

Take 8 Villagers off the Gold to Build Mountain Hall next to Town Center so it covers the most resources. When the hunt runs out, take your 5 Mounted Villagers back to mine Gold. Build Lumber Camp with the Wood Villager when you can.

Make Monk and take Relic, research Veterancy for Iron Pagoda and use only grassland horses to spawn them. Use them to harrass enemy villagers. Make Emissary from Town Center and take the nearest neutral market. You can now make mounted vills again! Rally Mounted Villager on Wood. Build Grassland when you can, build War Stable if the grassland is not under the influence of Great Pasture. Use Mounted Villager to make farms when you have excess wood. Build additional Monastery to cover next gather locations. If you have too much gold, buy Collective Hunting. Make some counter units if the Iron Pagoda are not enough to keep the enemy contained.

1. Making a couple of farms early with the Mounted Villager is good because of the Karma buff giving 75% extra gather rate. Mounted Villager collection rate from farms is a bit lower, but on the other hand you will spend only 75 Wood for a farm that is collected at 180 % efficiency (+buff). 2. After getting the Karma buff the second time, you can usually easily go for imperial age.

title: Delhi | Team games (aggro)
description: Aggressive build order to make time for your teammates to scale while the enemies are busy defending against you. Take advantage of the Dome of Faith and Compound of the Defender discounts to scale quicker while you make a big army.
author: Jockxtar
steps: 5 Villagers,then Wood. 1 Villager builds Mill,then House,then Berries. Rally,then Berries (up to 8). First Villager builds Mosque

Rally,then Wood (up to 11)

Once you get 80 Gold, move Gold Villager,then Food. Build Lumber Camp and House

If you are forced to stay in Feudal Age for longer, train additional Scholar so you don't float over 600 Gold, or trade it for Food at a Market for a faster Castle Age. It is also possible to make Venetian Trader if you miss-macro and have a big excess of Wood and Gold, but lack the Food to Castle Age. Although building more Barracks Archery Range Stable is usually a better choice.

Build Stable and start making Ghazi Raider nonstop. UPGRADES: Sanctity Piety All-Seeing Eye, Double Broadax Forestry Horticulture Survival Techniques Professional Scouts Specialized Pick. Make 1 Scholar from Dome of the Faith and garrison it inside of Stable.
Send at least 1 or 2 Ghazi Raiders to each enemy, don't attack always the same. If one of them builds Outpost, you can destroy it with (at least) 9 Ghazi Raiders after Iron Undermesh is researched.
Rally,then Food (until Castle Age )
As you get Wood, build 2 Blacksmiths. Research Iron Undermesh Bloomery Siege Engineering on the 1st one. and Steeled Arrow Fitted Leatherwork on the second one (order matters!)
Build Archery Range; Keep producing Ghazi Raider while you make Archer. Archer only role are to scare Spearman away and to build Palisade Wall, but you can eventually gather a decent mass of them.

Move both Scholar out to capture Sacred Site just as Sanctity is about to be completed. Don't fight too hard for Sacred Site. Use them as a distraction, forcing the enemies to move out of their base and creating more opportunitites to raid. Obviously the extra Gold is nice. If Sacred Site are contested frequently, put some Villager to gather Gold
Build Palisade Wall with Archer to defend your base or to block Relic. If you are playing in a closed map, you can even wall your opponents inside of their bases.
If you are getting raided by cavalry, build Barracks and train Spearman to defend and wall your base.
Make Scout to steal Deer from the opponent's side of the map, securing food and delaying the farm transition.
Make sure to have at least 2 of each Barracks Archery Range Stable by the time you age up to start producing Man-at-Arms + Crossbowman + Lancer at the same time that you get upgrades.
10 Food Villager,then Compound of the Defender,then Food. Rally,then Wood (30) for more Barracks / Archery Range / Stable and, later, Farm
See to the left. Reallocate villagers to something similar to this.
Train additional Scholar (but never going below 200 Gold, you will need it for units)

Try to extend this age for as much as possible, giving you time to get all the upgrades, a bunch of keeps to boost your economy and lots of scholars. Both Ghazi Raider and Man-at-Arms are a cost-effective frontline, but they can't be the core of your army. Ideal army composition: Lancer + Ghazi Raider + Archer + Tower Elephant (+ Spearman vs cavalry). OR. Lancer + Man-at-Arms + Mangonel + Tower Elephant (+ War Elephant + Scholar vs cavalry). Add Springald to counter enemy siege.

Research: Compound of the Defender,then Village Fortresses Slow-Burning Defenses Boiling Oil Court Architects. ; Lumber Preservation Fertilization Acid Distillation; Swiftness Herbal Medicine; Decarbonization Wedge Rivets Balanced Projectiles Insulated Helm Military Academy Forced March
Attack quickly and frequently to prevent the opponents from aging up to Imperial Age.
Build 3 Barracks, 5 Archery Ranges, 5 Stables with excess Wood. Build 1 Siege Workshop and garrison 1 Scholar inside. That will be enough until late Imperial Age.

Depending on how defensive the enemies are playing: Keep in your base to defend against a counterattack while you get upgrades. OR. Keep to protect key resources in the middle of the map. Build Stone Wall with infantry to protect your base. 3 Keeps is a good amount to stop gathering Stone. After that move Stone Villager,then Wood for more Farm
See to the left. Ideal economy (for now) should look like this
After technologies are done, garrison Scholar inside military buildings or to heal units during fights.

Hisar Academy for faster tempo (faster late game upgrades) and better food economy. Allows you to liberate population space for a bigger army. Palace of the Sultan good when constantly fighting/trading units with the opponents.
Make Scholar up to 20, but don't build more Mosque.

Ideal army composition: Man-at-Arms / Ghazi Raider + War Elephant + Tower Elephant / Sultan's Elite Tower Elephant + Scholar + Mangonel. Make Ghazi Raider instead of Man-at-Arms if enemies have a lot of Crossbowman. Add Springald to counter enemy siege. (Although your allies should make Culverin ). Use Ghazi Raider / Lancer to raid

Garrison Scholar inside Hisar Academy / Madrasa (including the 3 that spawn outside of it). Research Biology Incendiary Arrows Elite Army Tactics Siege Works Chemistry Court Architects. Research all upgrades.
After unit upgrades and economic technologies are completed: Garrison Scholar inside military buildings.
Build Stone Wall with your units as you push into the opponent's side of the map to protect reinforcements and control resources.
Military buildings proportions: 5 Barracks; 10 Archery Ranges; 15 Stables; 1 Siege Workshop

title: 1TC aggression or 2 TC by Valdemar1902 - OverlayTool
description: An effective way to play 1tc aggression. See notes for more tips and advice on strategy. OverlayTool: https://github.com/CraftySalamander/RTS_Overlay
author: schwazza
steps: Early game is all about a fast feudal age.

4 Villagers to Sheep. 1 Villager to Build Hunting Cabin on Wood,then 1 Sheep. 1 Villager to Build House,then Mining Camp Gold. Rally Villager to Sheep til Feudal Age. 4 Food Villager Build Feudal Age Kremlin

Once you have blacksmith techs you wanna get all the tier 1 upgrades as well. Add Professional Scouts if the opponent is low on food and deer are not secured. Then you can deny food and force farms. Survival Techniques if you go on boar/deer ( pairs well with Professional Scouts ). If you are pushing a 2nd Town Center you want to push with 3 rams at 11-12 minutes in. With a push like that, you always prioritise Archer mass to maximise your civ bonus of 20% extra wood. ________________________________________. Go castle age after taking a good fight vs 1TC aggro Opponent to finish off with upgrades and better units. If economy play from opponent, you go all-in. Technically, you can play 2nd TC as well after the stable with the macro from this build: https://aoe4guides.com/builds/usDmakzUrRAdgix7Di0P

-- 1 TC AGGRESSION ---. Rally Villager to Straggler Tree til 5. If 5 on Wood: Rally Villager to Food til 8. 4 Kremlin Villager Build Stable,then House,then Lumber Camp. Stable Knight. If 8 on Food: Rally Villager to Gold til 6

Double Broadax and Build Archery Range,then Archer. Build 2nd Archery Range and Blacksmith. If 6 on Gold: Rally Villager to Food. get Steeled Arrow Iron Undermesh. 4 Gold Villager,then Wood. get Wheelbarrow Horticulture Specialized Pick. if Deer not secured: get Professional Scouts and Scout from Hunting Cabin + Survival Techniques

-- 2nd TC VARIATION --. 4 Kremlin Villager Build Stable,then House,then Mining Camp Stone. Stable 1-3 Knights. If 8 Villagers on Wood: Rally to Stone til 2nd Town Center. 10+ Villager (all from Stone + Wood ) Build Town Center on Deer. Rally both Town Center to Gold. Castle Age High Trade House with makro: 25 Food / 15 Wood / 12+ Gold

Construct 2nd Town Center with 6x Villagers.

Keep majority of Villager on Wood as spamming production buildings grants you free units essentially driving the cost of the production building down to a fraction of the price. Wood also helps you afford an early Granary and Farm which means you never need to leave your base.

title: English | Dark Age farms opener
description: An optimized and flexible build order that takes advantage of English farm bonus from the very beginning of the game. Can transition into aggro, 2TC or FC with very competitive timings while also staying very safe.
author: Jockxtar
steps: Since we have Farm, you can send the Scout farther and take Sheep from the opponent's side of the map.
1 Villager,then Sheep. 3 Villagers,then Straggler Tree and drop once (we only need 30 Wood ). 2 Villagers,then Build Farm and Mill
First Villager,then Sheep
3 Villagers on Straggler Tree go to Sheep, after dropping 30 Wood. Rally,then House,then Mining Camp,then Gold (3)
Rally,then Sheep (3 more; total of 8)
Rally,then Wood (11)
4 Sheep Villager,then Build Feudal Age,then Wood
Council Hall: Better for aggro/tempo strategies. Abbey of Kings: Ideal to match fast Castle Age strategies. The King comes for free and can delay a bit the enemy timing.
Move 2 Sheep Villager,then Wood
Build Lumber Camp

Don't forget to build Outpost if you want to fight outside of your base. Army composition: Spearman + Longbowman. Add a handful of Man-at-Arms to tank for the Spearman. Longbowman are more cost efficient than Horseman against ranged units in Feudal Age
Research Double Broadax and Horticulture
Rally,then Sheep (5 more; total of 9 on Food )
Build House

Gradually Build Farm with Sheep Villager until 8. Always keep 1 Villager on Sheep. OR --- vs Delhi Sultanate French Jeanne d'Arc Knights Templar Mongols Byzantines ( Imperial Hippodrome ) ---. Save Wood for Barracks first. Then, build Farm
Build Archery Range or Barracks with excess Wood. (You want 1 of each)
Now you have 3 options:

----------------------------------------------- Aggro -----------------------------------------------. Rally,then Wood. Have 1 Barracks and either 2 Archery Ranges or Council Hall. Build Blacksmith and research: Steeled Arrow,then Iron Undermesh,then Siege Engineering. Keep your units in base until you have at least 4 Spearmen and 5 Longbowmen and the go out to harass the enemy base.

Gradually Build Farm with Wood Villager until you have a total of 16. This allows you to produce units nonstop with the production buildings mentioned before. If you want more units, make more farms. If you want to Castle Age, move 7 Villagers from Wood to Gold.

------------------------------------------------ 2TC ------------------------------------------------. Rally,then Stone (8). Research Specialized Pick. Move Gold Villager,then Stone. Make a small defensive army of Spearman + Longbowman while gathering Stone. Don't worry, you will have excess Food and Wood.
Rally,then Wood (X)
8 Stone Villager,then Build Town Center on Gold
After finishing Town Center: Rally,then Wood and Gold. Build Palisade Wall and more Farm. It's too late now for an all-in, but you can put some pressure while saving up resources to Castle Age.
You can have the resources to Castle Age by minute 8 even with a few Spearman / Longbowman to defend
Use 8 Farms Villager to Castle Age
Rally,then Wood (18)

King's Palace: If you rushed Castle Age, this landmark will help you scale your economy like crazy. Best option unless you are afraid of a potential all-in from your opponent. The White Tower: The safest choice. Ideal to protect your Farm even better.
Research Specialized Pick
Build 1 Stable if you built King's Palace.
Build Outpost and/or Keep to secure map control and buff your army. Army composition (early): Longbowman + Knight. Army composition (late): Man-at-Arms + Crossbowman + Horseman
Queue Knight ASAP and use them to raid and distract the opponent. If you have the King alive, move them together.
If you haven't already, build Archery Range (unless you have Council Hall )
Make a few Longbowman to counter enemy Spearman and protect your Knight
Get ready to transition into your mid-game composition by adding production buildings as follow: 4 Barracks; 4 Archery Ranges; 2 Stables. ( Council Hall counts as 2 Archery Ranges )
Upgrade Man-at-Arms to Castle Age and research Armor Clad

After reaching 18 Wood Villager, build 8 Farms with 8 of them. Keep repeating this process until you have 4 full packs of farms (total of 32 Villagers ). Then Rally,then Gold until you have 15 Villagers mining. Then Rally,then Wood and keep the cycle of adding Farm.

The goal during Castle Age is to apply a lot of pressure with our superior Food economy to damage our opponent and slow down their scaling while we get ready to Imperial Age. We can also add Battering Ram or Counterweight Trebuchet to finish our opponent if we have a big lead, but going Imperial Age is always ideal with English.
Remember to research Network of Citadels at The White Tower / Keep
TL;DR: If ahead: Wynguard Palace. If tied or behind: Berkshire Palace

Wynguard Palace: If you have secured map control in Castle Age and have access to Gold, this landmark will allow you to snowball the game and to compete with the strongest late game civilizations toe to toe. Berkshire Palace: If things are tied, this landmark is super good at securing map control and key resources. Also, if you are behind and at risk of getting all-in by your opponent, this will save you the game.

Army composition: Man-at-Arms / Wynguard Footmen + Longbowman / Wynguard Ranger. Add Horseman and Mangonel against Crossbowman. Add Handcannon Ashigaru against Knight. Add Spearman against Knight + Crossbowman armies
Immediately research Enclosures. Prioritize Longbowman and Man-at-Arms elite upgrades.
Build University: Elite Army Tactics,then Incendiary Arrows,then Silk Bowstrings
See to the left. Ideal economy balance should look like this:
Production balance: 10 Barracks; 10 Archery Ranges; 5 Stables; 3 Siege Workshops
Push forward slowly while building Outpost and Keep, slowly creeping closer and closer to the enemy base, so that you always benefit from the bonus attack speed.

After researching Incendiary Arrows and Silk Bowstrings at University, Longbowman / Wynguard Ranger counter siege units, even Mangonel, and their high base damage makes them quite competent against cavalry and armored units.
Produce Counterweight Trebuchet to destroy Keep and Stone Wall

Stable House

2nd Stable
Blacksmith (get Iron Undermesh Wedge Rivets,then Steeled Arrow Balanced Projectiles,then (sultans mamluks)

Upgrades ( Balanced Projectiles + Wedge Rivets ) are incredibly important and if you have fully upgraded archers, they last you very long and you forego the need for early expensive xbows. Don't be afraid to add a 2nd Blacksmith if necessary. The Camel Lancer + Archer comp is goated. Eco upgrades are also important. Get them as you can fit them in, but dont prioritise them over Blacksmith upgrades and Dervish.

title: Knights Templar | Serjeant aggro
description: Build order for a strong Feudal Age tempo/aggro strategy. Ideal to take map control and neutralize feudal knights. It works really well in team games if you spawn close to a French/JD enemy base to block their gold.
author: Jockxtar
steps: Rally,then House,then Mining Camp,then Gold (2)
Rally,then Sheep (7)
Rally,then Wood (5)
Rally,then Gold (3)
Feudal Age

Principality of Antioch: It's the best option vs French and Jeanne d'Arc since they have Royal Knight, which destroy Chevalier Confrere and Hospitaller Knight. Serjeant are a great unit to mass in Feudal Age, but kinda expensive and are soft-countered by Archer and static defenses. This makes all-ins with this commanderie very difficult. Still, forcing a civ that doesn't have a good Wood economy to make Archer early will put you at a great advantage.
Build Barracks
Produce 2 Spearmen and keep them defending your Gold. This will likely trick your opponent into thinking that you are going to play defensive. Use them to scare the enemy Scout away from your base.

Tip: Fortress don't grant bonus attack range to Serjeant until Desert Citadels is researched. Tip: The best positions for Fortress are: - Protecting Sacred Site. This protects our pilgrims when they are most vulnerable (since it's the closest point to the enemy base). And later in Castle Age will make us gain more Gold thanks to Treasure Towers. - Protecting our base. Place it at the front of the base, right next to the Barracks and Stable. This will allow us to protect our reinforcements and block the way to our economy. If you are playing a team game, you can also build it to protect your allies' base. - Chokepoints. Some maps have very obvious chokepoints that are key to hold for map control. - Important resources in the middle of the map such as large Gold and Stone veins or Boar. - In front of the enemy base. Very risky, but can allow you to snowball the game. Only do this if you already have a big military advantage.
Town Center,then Safe Passage. Rally,then Food (9)
Barracks: Produce groups of 2 Serjeants and 1 Spearman, then send all 3 together to enemy Gold. After the first group, research Spearman veterancy.
Build 2nd House
Rally,then Wood (7)
Build Stable to produce Horseman

In this army composition, Horseman 's role is to scare enemy Archer and to prevent them from massing into a deathball. Avoid engaging under Town Center or against Royal Knight with them. This strategy is not an all-in, we want to slowly gain advantage without committing to a risky fight.
Rally,then Food (16)

Try to block all Gold near the opponent's base. You don't need to kill Villager, just block the Gold and prevent them from massing Royal Knight or getting upgrades. You can send 1 Villager to build Outpost and block them for longer, but that's more dependant on the spawn of the Gold vein.
Build Blacksmith. Order of upgrades: Iron Undermesh,then Bloomery

Select 8 Food Villager and send them to closest Deer or Boar. If you don't see the enemy Royal Knight, keep a few Spearman and Serjeant near them. The other 8 Food Villager will finish Sheep and then go to Berries
Research Survival Techniques and Wheelbarrow with excess Gold.
Rally,then Gold (5)
Once you save 150 Wood, build 2nd Barracks. Stop making Spearman if the opponent is no longer making cavalry units.
If you ever float over 200 Food, reasearch Sanctuary on Town Center
Now you have two options:
With the Stone build a 2nd Town Center and/or a Fortress to boost economy and/or secure map control.
After getting the 10 Villagers on Stone, change Rally,then Wood (X) and start making farms to eventually age up to Castle Age.
If you see an opportunity to further punish your opponent and start floating Wood, research Siege Engineering. Build Battering Ram and focus Outpost and Archery Range.
If you don't want to be so aggressive, build Farm and research Horticulture, or build Palisade Wall and Outpost to protect your base. This extra Food will allow you to finally age up to Castle Age.

Angevin Empire: Heavy Spearman are amazing against Feudal Age armies that rely on cavalry. Going for these will allow you to close up the game in early Castle Age against civilizations like French, Jeanne d'Arc and Rus, since their Archer will become useless and they will have no way to protect their Knight. On top of that, they benefit greatly from Principality of Antioch passive bonus. Kingdom of Castile: Genitour are ultra specific counter units. Good choice against Ayyubids Abbasid Dynasty Rus Mongols Japanese if they are doing mounted cavalry units, which are the best counters to Serjeant. It would not be crazy to play for a Sacred Site victory given that we have been slowing down the game's pace considerably up to this point, but that's very dependant on the map. Republic of Genoa: Genoese Crossbowman are very strong against pretty much any unit, but are specially strong against melee infantry. Their biggest counter are Horseman and Archer. Since our opponent probably has the latter in high numbers already, they are not the most cost efficient unit we can make. Still, the bonus +30% Gold generated by pilgrims is very strong.
TL;DR: Angevin Empire on on on Kingdom of Castile on Republic of Genoa

Angevin Empire Army composition: Heavy Spearman + Serjeant + Horseman + Mangonel. Kingdom of Castile Army composition: Spearman + Serjeant + Genitour + Templar Brother. Add Mangonel if opponent has too many ranged units for your Genitour to handle
If you chose Angevin Empire, add more Barracks, Stable and 1 Siege Workshop
See to the left. Economy should look like this

If you chose Kingdom of Castile, add 2 Archery Ranges and more Barracks. Genitour breakpoints (on equal Blacksmith upgrades): 6 against Castle Age Archer and Crossbowman. 8 against Horse Archer, Mangudai and Onna-Musha. 10 against Desert Raider. 12 against Camel Archer
See to the left. Economy should look like this
Try to keep a steady amount of 30 to 40 Serjeants to snowball the fights. Be careful to not have them directly engaging Knight or Crossbowman without the support of the appropiate counters.
Don't forget to research Treasure Towers and to build a Fortress near the Safe Passage Sacred Site.
This build order is meant to close games before reaching the late game, but here are some tips anyways.

Kingdom of Poland: Szlachta Cavalry are an insane unit, extremely strong against all ranged units due to their high armor, bonus damage vs light infantry and mobility. The only problem is that your economy might be a bit too weak to consistently produce them. The passive bonus is also super good for Horseman, that alone makes it the best choice for this build. Republic of Venice: Condottiero benefit a lot from the bonus damage from Principality of Antioch, but they serve a very similar purpose to Serjeant. It also unlocks Venetian Trader though, which can boost our Gold eco significantly. Teutonic Order: Teutonic Knight are a solid frontline, but they are countered by Crossbowman just like the rest of our army. The armor debuff is always a decent bonus, but it only truly shines with high attack speed, low damage per hit units like Archer, Man-at-Arms, Horseman, Chevalier Confrere, Hospitaller Knight
TL;DR: Kingdom of Poland on Republic of Venice on Teutonic Order
Try to finish the age up with at least 2000 Gold for upgrades
Army composition: Heavy Spearman + Serjeant + Horseman + Szlachta Cavalry + Springald
Prioritize elite upgrades for Heavy Spearman, Serjeant and Horseman; and University upgrades.
See to the left. Economy should look like this
University: Elite Army Tactics,then Brigandine,then Biology. Dont' forget to research Fanaticism at Monastery and Roller Shutter Triggers at Siege Workshop
Finish the Farm transition and research Precision Cross-Breeding. You will need a lot of Food
With Knights Templar it's always good to have excess Food, since you can trade it for Gold very efficiently thanks to Lettre de Change
Add Springald to have a proper backline to support your cavalry units.
If you can't brute force your way into the enemy base, add Counterweight Trebuchet and research Counterweight Defenses, Geometry and Siege Works
